Subject: SSO incident — preliminary IR debrief and evidence delivery

Hi Sana / Acme team —

Thank you for flagging this. Below is a concise debrief and the link to the evidence bundle for your auditor. We are treating this as a minor availability incident (no confirmed data exposure).

Summary (what happened)
- Window: 2026-11-14 09:05–09:10 PST
- Symptom: intermittent 502s when exchanging auth codes at /oauth/callback
- Root cause (prelim): a race condition in our session-store refresh logic under a brief load spike where two concurrent callback requests attempted to refresh the same session token. In some cases, the token refresh path threw a transient error that surfaced as a 502 to the client.

Impact
- Affected requests: estimated 0.18% of auth transactions during the five-minute window (~320 requests)
- User impact: authentication failures that were resolved by client retries; no persistent account lockouts observed
- Data exposure: no evidence in logs or trace spans of token leakage or unauthorized access.

Remediations applied
- Immediate: tightened concurrency guard in session-store code and rolled a hotfix at 09:22 PST (deploy-events-20261114.log attached).
- Follow-up: scheduled a fix to the session refresh logic with a full test coverage change (patch queued for next release).

Evidence bundle (sealed):
- ir_summary_20261114.pdf (executive summary + checklist)
- auth-logs-20261114.zip (request/response snippets, checksums attached)
- sso-trace-20261114.ndjson (trace spans)

Download: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_share_link
Checksum (bundle): SHA256: 8f4d...7c91

If your auditor needs a PII-only redaction or a signed notarized package, let us know and we will coordinate with Legal and Compliance. We can also provide a short call to walk through the artifacts — propose Monday 11/16 10:00–10:30 PST if that works.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
